chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: Church music and jazz
summary: Smith links jazz rhythm to Holiness churches in Dallas and describes big church bands and choirs in Fort Worth and Tulsa.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Do you think that there's much musical connection between
Buster Smith - 107
the music of the church and Jazz? Do you think that's how Jazz got started? Is it a big influence on the beginnings of Jazz?

Well, yeah, I think so. Yeah. I know the rhythm come out of the church. Some of the rhythm, it comes out of the Holiness church. I heard bands in nineteen and twenty-five...twenty-four...in a big Holiness church up in North Dallas. It had trombone and saxophone and trumpets and all of that stuff, and drums and all of that in there. But the other church, it didn't have nothin' but organ and piano. But now they all pickin' it up.
You're getting full bands in churches.

Yeah. In Fort Worth, they got a great big band, you got fiddles and everything, Yeah, a big brass section. Down in Fort Worth. At G.R. Roberts, up there in Tulsa, you got a band there and a big choir. A choir and a band, and they got some great arrangements. Make Basie sound like Ellington(?).
You're kidding.

Heh-heh, it sure do! Whoever it is... I don't know who is doing that arranging, but he's out of sight. He sure is. And one of our best piano players he had -- Jimmy Smith. He's done joined the church. He's been in the church now about five or six years.
Does he not play Jazz at all now?
No. He only plays a little bit in the church.
Buster Smith - 108
That's Jimmy Smith, the organ player?

No. This is another Jimmy Smith. This is Jimmy Smith from Memphis, Tennessee. He used to play with Red Calhoun's band. He's a great piano player. A little-bitty old short fellow. Play a whole lot of piano.
You see, one of the things that has impressed me... I've been to a few Black churches in the States from time to time. I really enjoy it.
Uh-huh.

And one of the things I get off on is that the congregation is responding to the lead that the pastor gives, rather in the same way that musicians might back a soloist in a band. It's as if the congregation is doing little fill-ins and things like little riff figures behind...
Yeah.
And it carries the music along in this wonderful rhythmic, dynamic way.
Yeah. Oh yeah.
It sounds like Jazz to me.

Yeah, yeah. Some of these little-bitty churches over here, especially on ...(?)... over there in West Dallas, they've got them piano players that ain't playing nothing but the regular blues, with the people singing and clapping their hands.
